summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 5 upside misses — EDV.L +7%, FRES.L +7%, ANTO.L +6%, WEIR.L +5%, MTX.DE +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (BA.L -5%, RHM.DE -5%, TTE.PA -4%, SHELL.AS -4%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: EDV.L (+7.21%) — Gold spot surged to ~$4,300/oz near record highs on 2026-06-16 (momentum from prior session's US-Iran peace deal rally), triggering a broad gold-miner sector rally that lifted EDV.L +7.21%. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — EDV.L is a FTSE 250 mid-cap gold miner (metals/mining sector). The move was entirely sector/commodity-driven by XAU/USD spot price action, not a company-specific signal any equity momentum or mean-reversion screener would surface.

top_movers.catalyst: Gold spot surged to ~$4,300/oz near record highs on 2026-06-16 (momentum from prior session's US-Iran peace deal rally), triggering a broad gold-miner sector rally that lifted EDV.L +7.21%.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — EDV.L is a FTSE 250 mid-cap gold miner (metals/mining sector). The move was entirely sector/commodity-driven by XAU/USD spot price action, not a company-specific signal any equity momentum or mean-reversion screener would surface.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a gold-miners satellite screener that flags LSE metals/mining names when XAU/USD 1-day return exceeds +1.5% AND name-level volume is ≥1.2× 20-day avg; size positions at half normal risk given commodity-beta exposure.

top_movers.catalyst: Silver spot surged ~3.5% on pre-FOMC rate-hold positioning (97% probability priced) ahead of incoming Fed Chair Warsh's debut meeting; Fresnillo, world's largest primary silver producer, amplified the commodity move with ~2× equity beta.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. FRES.L is a FTSE 100 pure-play precious metals miner whose daily returns track XAG/XAU spot price with high equity beta; the bot's momentum and mean-reversion strategies do not cover commodity-regime-driven names and carry no precious-metals sector sleeve.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a commodity-equity satellite trigger: when XAG/USD intraday move exceeds +2% by 09:30 BST, scan FTSE350 miners for silver/gold beta >1.5 and fire a long signal — this rule would have flagged FRES.L at the open today without altering existing equity filters.

top_movers.catalyst: US-Iran interim peace agreement signed 2026-06-16 boosted risk sentiment; LME copper surged ~1.2% to ~$13,650/t, lifting ANTO.L +6.08% as the FTSE 100's largest pure-play copper proxy.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ANTO.L is a large-cap FTSE 100 copper miner. The move was a macro commodity catalyst (geopolitical de-escalation → copper spike) that materialised at open, making pre-market equity signal positioning impossible for a reactive bot.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a commodity-proxy trigger: when LME copper front-month gaps >+1% vs prior close, auto-admit top-3 LSE copper miners by market cap (inc. ANTO.L) into the momentum universe for that session with a 2× ATR stop.

top_movers.catalyst: US-Iran peace deal (June 15) reopened Strait of Hormuz, sent gold above $4,300 and sparked a FTSE 100 mining-sector rally; Weir Group, as the leading hard-rock mining equipment OEM, followed miners higher with a one-session lag.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: Weir is classified as Industrials/mining-equipment, not a pure-play miner, so sector screens tracking Rio Tinto, Antofagasta, and Anglo American do not extend to OEM equipment proxies. The move also arrived a day after the primary commodity surge, limiting pre-market signal for n
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'mining-capex proxy' sub-universe (Weir, Metso, Sandvik, Epiroc) to the mining momentum strategy, triggered when the FTSE mining sub-index gains ≥3% in a single session, releasing these names for next-day momentum entry.

top_movers.catalyst: ECB's 25bp rate hike on 11 Jun (first since 2023, effective 17 Jun) repriced European bank NIM expectations; DBK.DE extended its post-announcement rally as sector tailwinds accumulated through the week.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's screened universe. Macro-aligned strategies (macro-aligned-hmm, macro-aligned, regime-router) likely express ECB rate-sensitivity via broad financials ETFs rather than single European bank names; DBK.DE was absent from their single-name pick list.
top_movers.suggestion: Add top Euribor-sensitive DAX banks (incl. DBK.DE) to macro-aligned-hmm's universe with an entry gate: ≥+2% close-to-close within 3 sessions of an ECB rate-decision date flagged in the macro calendar.

top_movers.catalyst: European risk-on rally on Iran conflict peace-deal reports lifted DAX aerospace names; no MTU-specific announcement — macro/sector rotation into high-quality industrials.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — MTU Aero Engines is a DAX large-cap (~€17B) in aerospace/defense. Move was macro/geopolitical (Iran de-escalation reports); no company-level catalyst, so news-reactive and momentum filters had no signal to act on pre-open.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a European aerospace/defense macro-overlay universe (DAX A&D names incl. MTX.DE) that activates on broad geopolitical risk-off→risk-on reversals, gated by a ≥3% same-day STOXX Aerospace & Defence index move as the entry trigger.

top_movers.catalyst: UK Defence Secretary Healey resigned 12 Jun over underfunded Defence Investment Plan (2.68% GDP vs targets), raising contract-pipeline uncertainty; Monday selloff extended Friday's 1.75% fall into a 4.74% two-day drawdown.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. BA.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap whose move was driven by a UK government political catalyst (ministerial resignation), requiring macro pre-event positioning rather than the company-level momentum or earnings signals the bot screens for.
top_movers.suggestion: If shorts are available, add a UK-defence-policy event gate: senior MoD ministerial resignation or GDP-spend pledge cut ≥0.1pp triggers a short screen on top-5 FTSE defence names at next-session open within 30 min. If long-only, no-op.

top_movers.catalyst: Defense sector de-rating: Q1 2026 miss (€1.94B vs €2.28B est) + Ukraine peace-talk progress drove JPMorgan/Deutsche Bank downgrades; RHM continues multi-week slide from €2,008 52-wk high.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — RHM.DE is a €56B Xetra defense mega-cap in multi-month reset. Defense sector likely excluded by sector filter; macro-driven selloff requires short capability, not name-level long signals.
top_movers.suggestion: (no actionable change — capturing this requires shorting a defense mega-cap outside current universe and risk tolerance; adding RHM.DE long-only would increase exposure to an ongoing sector drawdown).

top_movers.catalyst: US-Iran peace deal announced ~Jun 15 reopened Strait of Hormuz, erasing geopolitical risk premium and sending Brent crude down ~5% to ~$83/bbl; TotalEnergies fell in lockstep as an oil-price-beta major.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. TTE.PA is a CAC 40 large-cap integrated energy major whose move was a pure macro oil-price shock from an overnight geopolitical headline — no intraday technical signal could have preceded the gap; pre-open positioning was the only viable entry.
top_movers.suggestion: Add Brent-futures daily return as a universe-gate signal: when Brent moves ≥3% overnight, auto-include top-5 European energy names (TTE.PA, SHEL.L, BP.L, ENI.MI, REPSOL.MC) in the next-open scan with a sector-shock short-side allowance.

top_movers.catalyst: Shell suspended its $3B share buyback (Jun 12–Jul 14) due to ARC Resources securities-law constraints, removing ~$1B/month of mechanical demand support from a €197B market-cap stock.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — mega-cap EU energy major likely excluded by sector or size filters. The buyback-halt catalyst was filed Jun 12; news-reactive strategies relying on post-open momentum signals missed the ensuing multi-day drift.
top_movers.suggestion: Expand EU large-cap energy universe and add a buyback-suspension trigger (6-K / RNS keyword scan); halting a $1B+/qtr program creates predictable multi-day drift suitable for a news-reactive mean-reversion entry at next-day open.
